pl_icon__domestic_sales.note: Bare 'Domestic', the usual row caption under 'Sale of products', is deliberately not aliased. The same bare word labels the indigenous half of raw-material and stores consumption splits, so it would bind a cost row to revenue. Segment-note rows such as 'India' or 'Within India' include other operating revenue, so they are not this figure. Expect this line to be filled by the model or by a note_source part (row_caption_any ^\s*domestic under a revenue-note title), not by a caption.
pl_icon__domestic_sales.definition: Sales of products and services to customers in India for the year, before excise duty. Ind AS filings print one face row, 'Revenue from operations'; the domestic/export split is in its note ('Sale of products - Domestic', 'Sale of services') or in the disaggregation of revenue / geographical segment note ('Within India'). Indian GAAP prints it in the 'Revenue from operations' note. Where only total sale of products is given with no geographical split, the whole is domestic. Other operating revenue (scrap, export incentives, job work) belongs to pl_icon__other_recurring_operating_income.
exclude_criteria: Other operating revenue such as scrap sales and export incentives

pl_icon__export_sales.note: Bare 'Export'/'Exports' is not aliased: it also labels rows under 'Earnings in foreign exchange' and 'CIF value of imports/exports'. 'Export of goods calculated on FOB basis' is a different figure (FOB, not invoice value) and is vetoed. Like domestic sales, this is mostly a note split left to the model or a note part.
pl_icon__export_sales.definition: Sales of products and services to customers outside India for the year, including deemed exports, before excise duty. Printed in the 'Revenue from operations' note ('Sale of products - Export', 'Export sales') or the geographical disaggregation ('Outside India'). Export incentives, duty drawback and RoDTEP/MEIS benefits are not sales: they are pl_icon__other_recurring_operating_income.
exclude_criteria: Export incentives, duty drawback, RoDTEP and MEIS benefits

pl_icon__gross_sales_total.note: Bare 'Sales' is the gross figure when excise is printed beneath it. When no excise line is printed, gross equals net, so it is still right. 'Sale of services' is not aliased (see unplaced). This is a calculated line: if the model fills only one of domestic/export, the partial sum replaces the printed figure (backend/app/services/rollups.py:342, 446-449).

aliases: Excise duty on sale of goods
Excise duty on sale of products
pl_icon__excise_duty.note: Revised Schedule VI faces print 'Less: Excise duty'. Normalisation does not strip 'Less:' (mapping.py:713-761, and no step in row_reconstruct.py:1640-1652), so the commonest face spelling will not bind. That needs a pipeline step, not a decorated alias. 'Excise duty on increase/(decrease) in stock' is an inventory adjustment and is vetoed. GST deducted in a gross-to-net reconciliation is not aliased (unplaced).
pl_icon__excise_duty.definition: Excise duty included in gross sales and deducted to reach net sales: the 'Less: Excise duty' row of an Indian GAAP P&L or revenue note, or the 'Excise duty' expense row of an Ind AS P&L for periods before GST (July 2017). Positive magnitude. GST is never included in revenue and is not this line.

pl_icon__net_sales.note: 'Revenue from operations (net)' is not net sales because it includes other operating revenue. It goes to total_operating_income and is vetoed here. This is calculated: a lone excise figure with no domestic/export would make the rollup compute -excise over a printed 'Net sales' (rollups.py:446-449).

aliases: Other recurring income incidental to main business
pl_icon__other_recurring_operating_incom.note: For a job-work processor, job-work income is its main revenue (sales), not incidental income. 'Job work charges' without 'received' is the expense caption and sits on line 16, so a revenue note printing bare 'Job work charges' for income would bind wrongly. That is rare.
pl_icon__other_recurring_operating_incom.definition: Operating income incidental to the main business: the 'Other operating revenue(s)' rows of the 'Revenue from operations' note - sale of scrap, export incentives, duty drawback, RoDTEP/MEIS, processing and job-work income, hire of equipment. 'Sale of services' printed beside 'Sale of products' is the business's own revenue and belongs to domestic or export sales, not here. Not 'Other income' (interest, dividends, disposal gains, fair-value gains), which is non-operating.
exclude_criteria: Interest, dividend and fair-value income in 'Other income'

aliases: Revenue from operations (net of excise duty)
pl_icon__total_operating_income.note: 'Revenue from operations (gross)' includes excise and has no ICON line (unplaced). Because this line is calculated, its face row is not decomposed (backend/app/stages/map_ontology.py:1145), so the note rows (Sale of products, Other operating revenue) do not publish. Lines 1, 2 and 7 stay with the model. The printed total is kept while no component is filled (rollups.py:340-343, 446-449).

aliases: Cost of raw materials and components consumed
Cost of raw materials & components consumed
pl_icon__raw_materials.note: Dropped the draft's bare 'Raw materials': it is the inventory caption and the row label under 'CIF value of imports', both different figures. This is calculated: if the model fills only one of imported or indigenous, the partial sum replaces the printed figure (rollups.py:342, 446-449). Purchases of stock-in-trade cannot be added here (see unplaced).

pl_icon__raw_materials_imported.note: The draft's bare 'Imported' also appears under stores and spares consumption and under CIF value of imports (raw materials, components, capital goods): three different figures. A better route is a note_source part: note_title_any imported\s+and\s+indigenous, row_caption_any ^\s*imported, reading the value column, not the % column.
pl_icon__raw_materials_imported.definition: Imported raw materials and components consumed in the year: the 'Imported' row of the 'Value of imported and indigenous raw materials consumed' table (with its percentage), printed in or after the 'Cost of materials consumed' note. Not CIF value of imports, which measures purchases. Leave empty if the filing gives no imported/indigenous split.

pl_icon__raw_materials_indigenous.note: The draft's bare 'Indigenous' also labels the stores-and-spares split, so it is dropped. Use the same note_source part with ^\s*(?:indigenous|domestic).
pl_icon__raw_materials_indigenous.definition: Indigenous raw materials and components consumed in the year: the 'Indigenous' row of the 'Value of imported and indigenous raw materials consumed' table. Where the filing prints only 'Cost of materials consumed' with no split, the whole consumption is indigenous and that total is cited.

aliases: Consumption of stores and spare parts
Consumption of stores, spares and consumables
pl_icon__other_spares.note: 'Stores, spares and packing materials' is vetoed because packing usually goes with materials. These rows sit in the 'Other expenses' note, so they publish only through decomposition of a face 'Other expenses' row bound to sga_others (map_ontology.py:1138-1161).
pl_icon__other_spares.definition: Stores, spares and consumables consumed in manufacture: 'Consumption of stores and spares', 'Stores and spares consumed', 'Packing materials consumed' in the 'Other expenses' (Ind AS) or 'Manufacturing expenses' (Indian GAAP) note. Not raw materials, not repairs.

pl_icon__power_and_fuel.note: 'Electricity charges' is not aliased: for a trader or service company it is office electricity, which is SG&A.
pl_icon__power_and_fuel.definition: Power and fuel consumed in manufacture: the 'Power and fuel' row of the 'Other expenses' or 'Manufacturing expenses' note. Not office electricity of a trading or service company, which stays in pl_icon__sga_others.
exclude_criteria: Office electricity of a non-manufacturing company

pl_icon__direct_labour.note: Schedule III prints one 'Employee benefits expense' for factory and office staff. That caption goes to line 24, the analyst convention when the filing does not split it, and only explicit factory captions land here. Bare 'Wages', 'Labour charges' and 'Contract labour charges' follow the CMA convention. In a service or EPC company, 'Labour charges' can be sub-contract cost. When a face 'Employee benefits expense' bound to line 24 cites a note that prints a separate 'Wages' row, decomposition carves the wages here (map_ontology.py:1195-1245).
pl_icon__direct_labour.definition: Factory labour: 'Contract labour charges', 'Labour charges', 'Wages' printed in the 'Other expenses' or 'Manufacturing expenses' note, or a factory wages row shown separately in 'Employee benefits expense'. When employee benefits expense is printed only as one total, it all belongs to pl_icon__salary_and_staff_expenses and this line is empty.

pl_icon__other_manufacturing_expenses.note: Old Schedule VI 'Manufacturing expenses' includes power, stores and labour, so it is broader than this line. It is vetoed here and placed on line 18, where decomposition can carve those items out.

pl_icon__processing_job_work_charges.note: 'Processing charges' on loans is a finance cost and is vetoed. Job-work income spellings are vetoed and go to line 7. A revenue note printing bare 'Job work charges' as income would bind here wrongly; decomposition has no sign check.
pl_icon__processing_job_work_charges.definition: Processing and job-work charges paid to outside parties for manufacture: 'Job work charges', 'Processing charges', 'Sub-contracting charges' in the 'Other expenses' or 'Manufacturing expenses' note. Construction or sub-contract costs of an EPC company printed as their own expense note are also cited here.

pl_icon__freight_and_transportation_char.note: ICON has one freight line, in cost of sales. Freight outward and forwarding is a selling cost but is also put here, because ICON SG&A has no freight line and the figure is still freight. Freight recoveries are vetoed.
pl_icon__freight_and_transportation_char.definition: Freight inward and transport of materials to the factory: 'Freight inward', 'Carriage inwards', 'Transportation charges' in the 'Other expenses' note. Freight outward / forwarding on sales is selling expense and belongs to pl_icon__sga_others.
exclude_criteria: Freight outward and forwarding on sales

aliases: Repairs and maintenance - Plant and machinery
pl_icon__other_manufacturing_expenses_ot.note: The 'Manufacturing expenses' figure is broader than this line. Binding it here lets decomposition (map_ontology.py:1138-1161) carve power, stores, labour, job work and freight into their own lines and keep only the remainder here. If the note does not reconcile, the whole figure stays here: total cost of sales is still right, only its split is wrong. Some analysts put packing materials with raw materials instead.
pl_icon__other_manufacturing_expenses_ot.definition: The remaining manufacturing rows of the 'Other expenses' or 'Manufacturing expenses' note: repairs to plant and machinery, factory rent, insurance of plant, testing and inspection, other manufacturing expenses. Only rows that are clearly factory costs and that no other cost-of-sales line claims.

aliases: Depreciation on property, plant and equipment
Depreciation of property, plant and equipment
pl_icon__depreciation.note: The combined face row 'Depreciation and amortisation expense' is placed here, following the CMA convention that the depreciation line carries D&A when it is not split. Decomposition carves the cited note's 'Amortisation of intangible assets' row to line 20 and keeps the rest here, so nothing is counted twice. 'Depreciation, amortisation and impairment' is vetoed because it includes impairment. map_ontology.py:849-853 forces PPE-note rows captioned 'Depreciation of property, plant and equipment' into the P&L gate, so that alias also binds the movement-table charge row in the note pass. That binding only shows in the Notes view; it does not publish.
pl_icon__depreciation.definition: Depreciation charged for the year on property, plant and equipment, investment property and right-of-use assets: the depreciation rows of the 'Depreciation and amortisation expense' note, or the 'Depreciation for the year' row of the property, plant and equipment / fixed assets note. When the face prints only 'Depreciation and amortisation expense' and no split exists, cite that row. Amortisation of intangibles is pl_icon__amortization.

pl_icon__amortization.note: Amortisation of borrowing costs, processing fees or premium is a finance cost, and amortisation of a government grant is income; all are vetoed. Any caption containing 'depreciat' is vetoed so a combined D&A row can never bind here.
pl_icon__amortization.definition: Amortisation of intangible assets for the year (software, technical know-how, licences): the amortisation row of the 'Depreciation and amortisation expense' note or the 'Amortisation for the year' row of the intangible assets note. Not depreciation of right-of-use assets.

pl_icon__changes_in_inventory.note: '(Increase)/decrease' and 'Increase/(decrease)' normalise to the same text because punctuation is stripped (mapping.py:759). An alias therefore cannot tell their signs apart; the definition must tell the sign stage that a stock build is negative. Excise on stock movements is vetoed (unplaced).
note_terms: changes in inventories of finished goods work in progress and stock in trade
pl_icon__changes_in_inventory.definition: 'Changes in inventories of finished goods, work-in-progress and stock-in-trade' as printed on the face: positive for a decrease (a charge), negative for an increase. Not closing inventory and not raw-material movements, which are inside materials consumed.

pl_icon__total_cost_of_sales.note: These aliases need alias_matching enabled. Ind AS Schedule III requires by-nature presentation, so this caption is rare in India. This is calculated: any single component, for example depreciation, replaces the printed figure (rollups.py:342, 446-449).

aliases: Total selling, general and administrative expenses
pl_icon__sga_expenses.note: Even the kept caption is replaced when line 24 is filled from a separate face row. Move it to sga_others too if the template keeps a plain SUM rollup here.

aliases: Payments to and provisions for employees
Salaries, wages, bonus and other allowances
Contribution to provident and other funds
Contribution to provident fund and other funds
Contribution to provident fund & other funds
Expense on employee stock option scheme
pl_icon__salary_and_staff_expenses.note: 'Employee benefits expense' covers both Direct Labour (14) and Salary and staff (24). It is placed on 24 as the convention when factory wages are not split. That moves factory wages from cost of sales into SG&A but does not change operating profit. Bare 'Gratuity' and 'Bonus' are not aliased because they also caption provision and actuarial note rows.
note_terms: payments to and provisions for employees
pl_icon__salary_and_staff_expenses.definition: Employee benefits expense: salaries, wages and bonus, contribution to provident and other funds, gratuity, staff welfare - the 'Employee benefits expense' face row or the total of its note. Excludes directors' sitting fees and commission printed in 'Other expenses' and contract labour, which are separate lines.
exclude_criteria: Directors' sitting fees and commission in 'Other expenses'

aliases: Rates and taxes, excluding taxes on income
Rates & taxes, excluding taxes on income
pl_icon__rent_rates_and_taxes.note: Bare 'Rent' is the commonest expense row, but an Other-income note can print bare 'Rent' for rental income. If a face 'Other income' row is decomposed, that income row would land on this expense line. Rental-income spellings are vetoed. Under Ind AS 116, short-term lease expense goes to line 26.
pl_icon__rent_rates_and_taxes.definition: 'Rent' (short-term and low-value lease rent under Ind AS 116) and 'Rates and taxes' rows of the 'Other expenses' note, cited as components. Not lease liability interest or right-of-use depreciation.

aliases: Expense relating to short-term leases and low-value assets
Expense relating to short-term leases & low-value assets
pl_icon__lease_rentals.note: Under Ind AS 116 most lease cost is now right-of-use depreciation (line 19) plus interest on lease liabilities (unplaced), so this line is small. 'Hire charges' (equipment hire) follows convention.
pl_icon__lease_rentals.definition: Lease rentals or hire charges printed separately from rent in the 'Other expenses' note ('Lease rentals', 'Hire charges', 'Equipment hire'). Empty when only 'Rent' is printed; rent belongs to pl_icon__rent_rates_and_taxes.

aliases: Bad debts and advances written off
Expected credit loss on trade receivables
pl_icon__bad_debts.note: Provisions and ECL allowances are non-cash. They are put with write-offs per CMA convention; some analysts move them to non-operating non-cash (order 58). 'Allowance for doubtful debts' is also a balance-sheet contra caption, which the statement gate refuses. Recoveries and write-backs are vetoed.
pl_icon__bad_debts.definition: Bad debts written off and the provision / allowance for doubtful debts or expected credit loss charged in the year, from the 'Other expenses' note, cited as components. Not the closing allowance balance.

pl_icon__travelling_and_conveyance.note: Directors' travel is treated as travel.
pl_icon__travelling_and_conveyance.definition: 'Travelling and conveyance' expense from the 'Other expenses' note.

pl_icon__advertisement_and_sales_promoti.note: By-function 'Selling and marketing expenses' includes staff cost and is not aliased here (it goes to sga_others).
pl_icon__advertisement_and_sales_promoti.definition: 'Advertisement', 'Sales promotion', 'Business promotion' rows of the 'Other expenses' or 'Selling and distribution expenses' note.

pl_icon__commission_discount_and_service.note: Bare 'Commission' is not aliased: it is also commission income (traders, agents) and directors' commission (line 32). Under Ind AS 115, discounts are usually netted off revenue and will not appear as an expense.
pl_icon__commission_discount_and_service.definition: Selling commission, brokerage, discounts and service charges paid on sales from the 'Other expenses' or 'Selling and distribution expenses' note. Not directors' commission.

pl_icon__legal_and_professional_charges.note: Payment to auditors goes to line 33 and is vetoed here.
pl_icon__legal_and_professional_charges.definition: 'Legal and professional charges' / 'Legal and professional fees' from the 'Other expenses' note. Payment to auditors is pl_icon__auditors_remuneration.

pl_icon__directors_remuneration.note: Executive directors' pay is often inside 'Salaries' and only appears in the related-party note. No face row cites that note, so it is never decomposed and this line stays blank.
pl_icon__directors_remuneration.definition: Directors' sitting fees and commission to non-executive directors printed in the 'Other expenses' note, plus managerial remuneration only where printed separately from employee benefits expense. Remuneration already inside employee benefits expense is not cited again.

pl_icon__auditors_remuneration.note: Some notes print the 'Payment to auditors' subtotal and its 'Audit fee' sub-row in the same cited note. Both would bind here, so decomposition sums them, fails its arithmetic gate and declines (map_ontology.py:1072-1074). That failure is safe. Internal and cost audit fees go to professional charges.
pl_icon__auditors_remuneration.definition: 'Payment to auditors' / 'Auditors' remuneration' in the 'Other expenses' note: audit fee, tax audit, other services and reimbursement. Cite the row in 'Other expenses', or the total of its sub-note, not both.

pl_icon__sga_others.note: Schedule III face 'Other expenses' is not SG&A others: it contains power, stores, repairs, freight, rent, travel and more. Binding it here is what lets decomposition (map_ontology.py:1138-1161) carve the note rows into lines 12-33 and the non-operating lines, with only the unclaimed remainder left here. The split is refused, and the whole figure stays here, when the note does not reconcile or when two face rows carry this key (map_ontology.py:1175-1182). The operating-expense total is still right; the cost-of-sales/SG&A split is not. By-function 'Selling and marketing' and 'General and administrative' lines include their own staff costs.
pl_icon__sga_others.definition: Every remaining row of the 'Other expenses' note that no other ICON expense line claims: freight outward, repairs to buildings and others, insurance, communication, printing, CSR expenditure, donations, security, miscellaneous expenses. Cite each such row as a component; never cite the note total together with its rows. When the filing prints only 'Other expenses' with no note, that face row is cited here.
exclude_criteria: The 'Other expenses' note total when its rows are cited
Rows claimed by power and fuel, stores, job work, freight inward, rent, rates, bad debts, travel, advertisement, commission, legal, directors' and auditors' remuneration

pl_icon__total_operating_expenses.note: Schedule III 'Total expenses' includes finance costs and D&A, so it is not this figure (unplaced).

aliases: Operating profit before interest and finance charges
Operating profit before interest & finance charges
pl_icon__operating_profit_before_interes.note: 'Operating profit', 'EBITDA' and 'Profit before interest and tax' are not aliased. Indian usage varies: before or after depreciation, with or without other income. The Ind AS set's 'Operating profit' (is_pl__net_operating_profit, output_csv_indas_line_items.json:5914) is a different subtotal.

pl_icon__interest.note: Hazard: 'Finance costs' is the only common caption for this line, and the line is a calculated sum of 38 + 39 + 40. Bank charges usually sit in the Other-expenses note. If decomposition carves them onto line 40, the rollup becomes computable from bank charges alone and replaces the printed finance costs (rollups.py:342, 446-449), understating interest by the whole finance cost. Fix this in the template: role 'line' on this node publishes printed plus extra parts (rollups.py:463-472), which is the CMA reading. Otherwise drop line 40's aliases. Unsplit 'Interest expense' and 'Interest on borrowings' cover both 38 and 39 and are not aliased anywhere.

aliases: Interest on Fixed Loans / Term loans
Interest on term loans from banks
Interest on secured loans - term loans
pl_icon__interest_term_loans.note: The finance-cost note publishes nothing by itself: its face row 'Finance costs' is bound to a calculated line, and calculated lines are not decomposed (map_ontology.py:1145). This line needs the model or a note_source part. 'Interest on lease liabilities' is unplaced.
pl_icon__interest_term_loans.definition: Interest on term loans, debentures, vehicle loans and other long-term borrowings, and interest on lease liabilities, from the 'Finance costs' note. Not interest on cash credit or working-capital loans.
exclude_criteria: Interest on cash credit and working-capital loans

aliases: Interest on cash credit and overdraft
pl_icon__interest_working_capital_loans.note: 'Interest on short-term borrowings' can include related-party inter-corporate deposits; CMA still treats them as working capital. The note-only caveat on line 38 applies here too.
pl_icon__interest_working_capital_loans.definition: Interest on cash credit, working-capital demand loans, packing credit, bill discounting and other short-term borrowings from the 'Finance costs' note.
exclude_criteria: Interest on term loans, debentures and lease liabilities

pl_icon__bank_charges.note: These aliases are figure-correct but trigger the line 37 hazard: bank charges carved out of 'Other expenses' make the interest rollup replace the printed finance costs. Ship them only with the template fix described on line 37.
pl_icon__bank_charges.definition: Bank charges, loan processing fees, guarantee and LC commission and 'Other borrowing costs' from the 'Finance costs' note (or bank charges in 'Other expenses'). Exchange differences regarded as borrowing cost belong here too.

pl_icon__operating_profit_after_interest.note: Schedule III 'Profit before exceptional items and tax' includes other income, so it is not this figure. It belongs to the PBT block.

pl_icon__misc_income.definition: The remaining cash items of the 'Other income' note: miscellaneous income, rental income, insurance claims, net foreign-exchange gain. bs_icon__short_term_borrowings_related_p.definition: Short-term loans from directors, promoters, subsidiaries or other related parties in the current borrowings note.

bs_icon__share_application_money.note: The refundable portion is a liability (RSVI other current liabilities) and is vetoed. 'Money received against share warrants' is listed as unplaced (116).

bs_icon__foreign_currency_translation_re.note: 'Exchange fluctuation reserve' was not borrowed; some filings use it for other FX items. FCMITDA (the AS 11 para 46A debit balance) is vetoed and listed as unplaced.

bs_icon__minority_interest.note: The P&L attribution rows of the same caption are kept off by the statement gate, and the matrix columns of the changes-in-equity statement are never claimed.

bs_icon__quasi_equity.note: No filing caption is this figure. The candidate source rows ('Unsecured loans from promoters/directors') sit on 75 / 101, and moving them is a reviewer or model decision based on the sanction letter. Filling this line without also removing the amount from 75/101 double-counts it inside total liabilities.

bs_icon__net_worth_others.note: It will absorb money received against share warrants, share capital suspense, treasury shares (negative) and instruments entirely equity in nature (see unplaced).

bs_icon__net_worth.note: RSVI consolidated 'Shareholders' funds' EXCLUDES minority interest, which RSVI prints separately, so that alias understates when MI exists. 'Equity attributable to owners' is vetoed for the same reason. Once 118 moves to bs_top_level, bs_equity has no calculated closing line for section reconciliation, because net worth is extracted. The 'liabilities' veto names the conjunction ('equity and liabilities', 'liabilities & equity') rather than the word: 'Total equity' with the 'Liabilities' heading glued on by row reconstruction reads 'total equity liabilities', and that row IS net worth.

bs_icon__total_liabilities_and_net_worth.note: The RSVI bottom line is a bare 'TOTAL', which cannot be an alias. The draft's 'TOTAL LIABILITIES' is dropped and vetoed: in annual reports it means outside liabilities (104), and on bs_top_level both lines claiming it would be an unbreakable tie.

On an old Schedule VI or partnership balance sheet that row sits under 'APPLICATION OF FUNDS', a banner that resolves to no section (mapping.py:1058-1074), so the alias would bind long-term investments here. STRUCTURAL: this line is not a term of bs_icon__total_current_assets (keytable order 144 terms; workbook =ROUND(F79+F83+F84+...) skips F82). A figure published here never reaches Total current assets or Total assets.

aliases: Investments in units of mutual funds

note_terms: bank balances other than cash and cash equivalents

bs_icon__receivables.note: Non-current Ind AS 'Trade receivables' is kept off by the section gate (this line is bs_ca). The ICON label says 'incldg. bills purchased and discounted', but bills that were discounted and derecognised are NOT inside the printed figure.

bs_icon__domestic_receivables.note: Most filings print no split. The face figure then stays on bs_icon__receivables, and an analyst (or a derived 'total minus export' rung) has to fill this leaf.
bs_icon__domestic_receivables.definition: Trade receivables from customers in India due within six months, net of allowance for doubtful debts. Where the filing gives no domestic/export split, all current trade receivables are domestic. Receivables overdue more than six months are bs_icon__receivables_over_6_months.
exclude_criteria: Receivables overdue more than six months
Allowance for expected credit loss as a separate figure

bs_icon__export_receivables.note: Export incentives and duty drawback receivable are not trade receivables and are vetoed.
bs_icon__export_receivables.definition: Trade receivables from overseas customers, where the trade receivables note or its text states them.

bs_icon__deferred_receivables_due_within.note: Leave to the model or a reviewer. Do not alias 'Current maturities of long-term loans': that is a loan, not a receivable.
bs_icon__deferred_receivables_due_within.definition: Instalments of deferred-payment receivables falling due within one year.

bs_icon__inventory.note: rollups.py:446-449: a calculated subtotal can be computed from ANY child that is present. If only some inventory note rows bind (for example raw materials left unplaced), the partial sum replaces the printed total. That is why 'Raw materials' is placed on a leaf (indigenous) and not on the calculated raw-materials line.

bs_icon__inventory_raw_materials_importe.note: Bare 'Imported' is dropped because it binds any row so captioned. Block 1's pl_icon__raw_materials_imported carries the same two strings under is_pl. That is not a test tie (scopes differ), but in an uncited note (statement=None, map_ontology.py:838) both lines are claimants and declaration order picks the P&L line. That is the right answer for a consumption or CIF note.
bs_icon__inventory_raw_materials_importe.definition: Imported raw materials in inventory, where the 'Inventories' note splits imported and indigenous stock.

bs_icon__inventory_raw_materials_indigen.note: This can only be wrong in the imported/indigenous split, never in the raw-material or inventory total. Risk: an UNCITED note that prints a bare 'Raw materials' row (Schedule III Part II CIF value of imports, or the imported/indigenous consumption analysis) is matched with statement=None/section=None (map_ontology.py:835-855) and would bind here. A sub__ note part with note_title_any 'inventor' would remove that risk. Bare 'Indigenous' is dropped.
bs_icon__inventory_raw_materials_indigen.definition: Raw materials and components in inventory (including goods-in-transit) from the 'Inventories' note; all raw-material stock when no imported/indigenous split is given.

aliases: Stock-in-trade (in respect of goods acquired for trading)
bs_icon__finished_goods.note: Stock-in-trade is placed on FG by analyst convention.
bs_icon__finished_goods.definition: 'Finished goods' and 'Stock-in-trade' (traded goods) rows of the 'Inventories' note, including goods-in-transit.

bs_icon__other_consumable_spares.note: Block 1's pl_icon__other_spares carries 'Stores and spares', 'Stores, spares and consumables' and 'Consumable stores and spares' under is_pl. That is not a test tie. In an uncited consumption note the P&L line wins by declaration order, which is correct there. Loose tools and packing materials are not aliased (see unplaced).
bs_icon__other_consumable_spares.definition: 'Stores and spares', 'Packing materials', 'Loose tools' rows of the 'Inventories' note.

bs_icon__advances_to_suppliers.note: ICON wants advances to suppliers of raw materials, stores and spares; the printed row usually also covers service vendors. Capital advances are vetoed so they go to bs_icon__advances_to_suppliers_of_capital_goods.
bs_icon__advances_to_suppliers.definition: Advances to suppliers of raw materials, goods and services in 'Other current assets' or 'Short-term loans and advances'. Capital advances are non-current.

bs_icon__advance_payment_of_taxes.note: Ind AS 'Non-current tax assets (net)' under non-current assets cannot reach this bs_ca line (section gate). It falls to the bs_nca residual.
bs_icon__advance_payment_of_taxes.definition: 'Current tax assets (net)' or advance income tax / tax deducted at source (net of provision) shown as a current asset.

bs_icon__other_current_assets.note: Ind AS current 'Other financial assets' is NOT aliased. Binding a second face row to this parent defeats the one-face-row decomposition gate (map_ontology.py:278-325), and that caption mixes deposits, unbilled revenue and interest accrued. No captions, deliberately. This line is calculated and its last term is the section's catch-all, so a face caption bound here is REPLACED by the computed figure as soon as the sweep fills the catch-all (rollups.figures_as_shown: computed outranks printed). Measured on a Schedule III balance sheet: 'Other current assets' 270 bound here, Investments/Loans/Other financial assets 300 swept beneath it, and the line showed 300 - total current assets short by 270. Unbound, the face row is swept into the catch-all with the others and the group shows 570.

bs_icon__interest_receivable.note: Shares 'Interest accrued' with block 3's bs_icon__interest_accrued (bs_cl), whose LABEL that caption is. The section gate separates them on the face. In an unsectioned or uncited context the label owner wins (mapping.py:1722-1729), so the liability line takes it.
bs_icon__interest_receivable.definition: 'Interest accrued on deposits / loans' in other financial assets (current).

bs_icon__prepaid_expenses.definition: 'Prepaid expenses' in 'Other current assets' or 'Short-term loans and advances'.

bs_icon__retention_money_current_portion.note: The same captions are proposed on bs_icon__retention_money_non_current_portion (bs_nca), and only the section gate splits them. Where the banner resolves to nothing (old Schedule VI 'APPLICATION OF FUNDS', the partnership horizontal format), both pass and declaration order gives this line. Retention often sits inside trade receivables with no row of its own.

bs_icon__other_advances_recoverable.note: 'Other loans and advances' (the Revised Schedule VI L&A note '(e) Others') may itself include prepaid expenses or GST balances when they are not itemised, hence medium. 'Balances with government authorities' is left unaliased (see unplaced). Related-party and director loans are vetoed.
bs_icon__other_advances_recoverable.definition: Loans and advances to employees and other advances recoverable in cash or kind (current 'Loans', 'Short-term loans and advances').

bs_icon__total_current_assets.note: The CMA total will NOT equal the printed one. It omits bs_icon__current_investments (not among its terms) and anything the CMA moves to non-current (margin FDs, dues from directors, receivables over 6 months).
bs_icon__total_current_assets.definition: Total current assets on the CMA basis, as the template computes it: cash and bank balances, current investments and fixed deposits, receivables, instalments of deferred receivables, inventory, advances to suppliers, advance payment of taxes and other current assets. The 'Total current assets' face row is its printed figure; once the parts are read the computed figure replaces it, so the printed row is a cross-check.

bs_icon__gross_block.note: Keeping 'Gross Block' here would be a partial-sum trap. With CWIP bound and the leaf empty, rollups.py:446-449 would publish CWIP alone as gross block.
bs_icon__gross_block.definition: Gross block as the template computes it: the gross carrying amount of land, buildings, plant, machinery and right-of-use assets, plus capital work-in-progress.

bs_icon__land_building_plant_machinery.note: Schedule III face 'Property, plant and equipment', Revised Schedule VI 'Tangible assets' and 'Right-of-use assets' are NET of depreciation. All three are aliased: the label includes the ROU asset, and with accumulated depreciation blank Net Block is still right (the same convention as net PPE). Unaliased, the ROU face row was swept into the non-current catch-all. The gross figure is in the PPE note's 'Gross carrying amount ... As at 31 March' cell, which no caption alias can reach; it needs a note_source part that selects the column or measure. 'Gross carrying amount' is not aliased because the same row heads the intangibles and investment-property notes too. Parity caveat: line_item_matching.py:323-327 indexes LABELS as aliases, so the parity engine would give 'Gross block' to bs_icon__gross_block (its label owner). The runtime OntologyMatcher does not index labels (mapping.py:1685-1691) and gives it to this line.
bs_icon__land_building_plant_machinery.definition: Gross block of tangible fixed assets at the year end: the 'Gross carrying amount - balance at the end of the year' total of the property, plant and equipment / fixed assets note, plus the right-of-use assets gross block. When only net carrying amounts are printed, cite the net figure.

bs_icon__capital_work_in_progress.definition: 'Capital work-in-progress' closing balance (face row or its note).

bs_icon__accumulated_depreciation.note: Old Schedule VI prints 'Less: Depreciation'. 'Less:' is stripped neither by normalize_label (mapping.py:713-761) nor by the leading-numbering step (row_reconstruct.py:1562-1567), and aliases may not carry it, so that face row stays unmatched. Bare 'Depreciation' is not aliased because it is also the PPE note's charge-for-the-year row. In Ind AS PPE matrices 'Accumulated depreciation' is a block heading and the closing balance is an 'As at ...' row, which needs a note part. Investment-property notes print the same caption.
bs_icon__accumulated_depreciation.definition: Accumulated depreciation and impairment at the year end: the 'Accumulated depreciation - balance at the end of the year' total of the property, plant and equipment / fixed assets note, plus the right-of-use assets' accumulated depreciation.

bs_icon__group_loans_and_advances.note: 'Loans (and advances) to related parties' can include directors and KMP, which ICON keeps in dues from directors. In practice these are mostly group companies, hence medium. Group loans classified as current are refused by the bs_nca gate.
bs_icon__group_loans_and_advances.definition: Loans and advances to subsidiaries, associates and other group companies.

bs_icon__other_non_current_investments_a.definition: Non-current investments outside the group (equity, bonds, mutual funds held long term) and long-term loans not to group companies.

bs_icon__security_deposits.definition: 'Security deposits' (non-current) in other financial assets or long-term loans and advances.

bs_icon__fds_under_lien.definition: Margin money deposits and fixed deposits held as security / under lien against bank guarantees and letters of credit, current or non-current.

bs_icon__receivables_over_6_months.definition: Trade receivables outstanding for more than six months: the '6 months - 1 year', '1-2 years', '2-3 years' and 'More than 3 years' columns of the trade receivables ageing schedule (undisputed, considered good), cited as components.

bs_icon__retention_money_non_current_por.note: Same captions as the current-portion line; only the section gate separates them.

bs_icon__intangible_assets.note: Face figures are NET of amortisation, so this line holds net intangibles and bs_icon__accumulated_amortization is left unaliased; aliasing both would deduct amortisation twice. In old Schedule VI 'Miscellaneous expenditure' sits below 'Current Liabilities and Provisions', and that banner (current_liabilities) refuses this bs_nca line. Note component rows (software, trademarks) are deliberately not aliased, to avoid binding both the face row and the note rows.
bs_icon__intangible_assets.definition: Intangible assets including deferred tax assets, as the label says: the gross carrying amount at the year end of intangible assets (software, technical know-how, licences) from the intangible assets note, plus intangible assets under development, plus the 'Deferred tax assets (net)' and MAT credit entitlement rows - the CMA deducts all of them from tangible net worth. Cite each as a component. When only net intangibles are printed, cite net.

bs_icon__accumulated_amortization.note: Fill this only together with a gross-intangibles note part, both read from the same note.
bs_icon__accumulated_amortization.definition: Accumulated amortisation of intangible assets at the year end from the intangible assets note.

bs_icon__total_assets.note: Old and Revised Schedule VI print a bare 'TOTAL', which is too generic to alias. The CMA total excludes current investments, because they are not in Total current assets. Section: the keytable scopes this line bs_ca, while Ind AS scopes it ['bs_top_level'] so that no banner constrains it (mapping.py:1224-1243). bs_ca works on Schedule III because the row follows the current-assets banner.

cov_icon__contingent_liabilities.definition: The total of contingent liabilities not provided for in the 'Contingent liabilities and commitments' note: claims not acknowledged as debts, disputed taxes, guarantees, LCs and bills discounted. Capital commitments are not contingent liabilities.
